policy_title: Modernise House of Commons and Ban Paid Advisory Roles for MPs
stated: Labour will establish a new Modernisation Committee to reform House of Commons procedures, raise standards, and improve working practices. As an initial step, Labour will support an immediate ban on MPs taking up paid advisory or consultancy roles, and task the Committee with developing further restrictions to prevent MPs from roles that conflict with their constituents' interests.

source.quote: Labour will establish a new Modernisation Committee tasked with reforming House of Commons procedures, driving up standards, and improving working practices. Therefore, as an initial step, Labour will support an immediate ban on MPs from taking up paid advisory or consultancy roles. We will task the Modernisation Committee to take forward urgent work on the restrictions that need to be put in place to prevent MPs from taking up roles that stop them serving their constituents and the country.

bearing_set.reason: Banning paid advisory/consultancy roles for MPs and establishing standards enforcement directly bears on the integrity of democratic representation and the rule of law — MPs acting in the interest of paid clients rather than constituents is a conflict that undermines the democratic mandate, touching the 'voting & democratic rights' and 'due process & rule of law' indicators.

Perceived conflicts of interest among elected representatives are a documented driver of public distrust in political institutions; a binding ban on paid advisory roles plausibly moves the 'social trust' indicator by reducing a visible source of institutional delegitimisation.

membership_note: The Modernisation Committee itself is largely procedural/machinery-of-government, but the substantive ban on paid advisory roles earns real verdicts on democratic integrity (O9) and institutional social trust (O15). No material bearing on cost of living, healthcare, housing, tax, or other fundamentals.
